chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hassan al-Mu'adab narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahani narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, saying: Ja'far ibn al-Hassan ibn Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Abasi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Salami, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqeel, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, saying: I heard God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) mention several nobilities of Ali (peace be upon him). If even one of those nobilities were in all of humanity, it would suffice for them as a distinction.

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master.' He said: 'Ali is to me as Aaron was to Moses.' He said: 'Ali is from me and I am from him.' He said: 'Ali is to me like my own self; obeying him is obeying me, and disobeying him is disobeying me.' He said: 'War against Ali is war against God, and peace with Ali is peace with God.' He said: 'The friend of Ali is the friend of God, and the enemy of Ali is the enemy of God.' He said: 'Ali is God's Proof and His Caliph over His servants.' He said: 'Love for Ali is faith, and hatred for him is disbelief.' He said: 'Ali's party is God's party; his enemies are Satan's party.' He said: 'Ali is with the Truth and the Truth is with him; they will not separate until they meet me at the Pool.' He said: 'Ali is the divider of Paradise and Hell.' He said: 'Whoever parts from Ali has parted from me, and whoever parts from me has indeed parted from God, the Exalted.' He said: 'The followers of Ali are the successful ones on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.قَسِيمُ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ: the divider of Paradise and Hell
key_terms.كَهَارُونَ مِنْ مُوسَى: like Aaron was to Moses (indicating rank and proximity)

ai.seo_question: What are the key virtues and sayings of the Prophet regarding Imam Ali mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith in *al-Khisal* to establish the theological foundation of *Wilayah* by linking Imam Ali’s authority directly to the Prophet’s essence through the concept of *Mawla*. The narration emphasizes that Ali’s status is not merely political but ontological, equating obedience to him with obedience to God and the Prophet, thereby defining 'Shi'at Ali' as the true victors on the Day of Judgment. This collection of sayings serves as a cornerstone for Shia exegesis regarding the continuity of divine guidance after the Prophet.
